answer: A river pigment market charges a nonrefundable admission burn for each voting credential. At the jetty registry, a spent burn output can issue only one credential and cannot be claimed again. A farmer wanting a thousand voting identities must destroy a thousand entry fees; copying keys or receipts adds no seats. The fee must be paid in a scarce asset and cover any signup subsidy. This makes aliases costly, not impossible: a wealthy attacker can still buy influence, and legitimate newcomers bear the same fee.
